content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 3, 13, and 15. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 and SEI Views and Beyond. This unit focuses on viewpoints as reusable guidance.

A viewpoint defines how to construct a view for a recurring class of stakeholder concerns. It describes the audience, concerns, model kinds, notation, analysis techniques, and consistency checks that guide the view.

The important distinction is that a viewpoint is the recipe and a view is the resulting artifact for a specific system. This allows teams to reuse architectural thinking without pretending every system needs identical documentation.
Studio: create a small viewpoint definition for an API integration view, including stakeholders, concerns, notation, and validation questions.

concepts.name: Architecture viewpoint
concepts.description: Reusable guidance for creating views that address a set of stakeholder concerns.

concepts.name: Architecture view
concepts.description: A system-specific representation created according to a viewpoint to address stakeholder concerns.

concepts.name: Viewpoint concern
concepts.description: A concern that a viewpoint is designed to expose, analyze, or communicate.

concepts.name: Model kind
concepts.description: A category of model used in a viewpoint, such as context, component, deployment, data, or state model.
